newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Faulding expects improved U.S. result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Faulding expects improved U.S. result.

text.p: Pharmaceutical supplier F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Monday it expected its U.S. operations to provide improved profit contributions in the future as a result of a restructure during the past year.
Faulding earlier reported a 23.3 percent lower full year net profit of A$27.998 million.

"As a result of the restructure during the year, the U.S. operations are expected to provide improved profit contributions in future," Faulding chief executive officer Ed Tweddell said in a statement accompanying the results.

"Our future prospects in the U.S. are good following the significant improvement in profitability in the final quarter of the 1995/96 year due to the receipt of several long awaited new product approvals," he said.

He said its U.S. subsidiary Purepac now had more products awaiting U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval than at any other time in its history and Faulding Inc management are planning for significant growth in profitability in 1996/97.
In the same statement, chairman Alan McGregor said group net profit before abnormal items was A$35.4 million, three percent below 1994/95, but slightly ahead of expectations.
This was largely due to delays in receipt of new product approvals by Purepac and an increasing investment in business development activities, he said.

McGregor said the contribution from operations in China, where sales of A$25.9 million were recorded, was less than expected as a result of price competition and manufacturing issues and the Australian consumer business experienced a number of delays in new product launches.
